answer: Each identity plants one quartz seed in a shared orchard that only sprouts after a maturation slow as a glacier: thirty epochs of continuous, distinct, useful work, each epoch's work verified by a different stranger. A clone farm cannot fast-forward time or copy a neighbour's harvest, because every seed carries its owner's key and every epoch demands fresh work. If an identity goes quiet for one epoch, its seed freezes and the count restarts. Running a hundred fakes means tending a hundred seeds through a hundred separate slow winters, each costing its own labour, with no harvest shared.
